s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower urinary tract symptoms with hematuria and urethral mass
salient_findings: Nocturia two to three times per night
Microscopic hematuria (3–5 red cells per high-power field)
key_facts: 53-year-old man
3-year history of slowly progressive lower urinary tract symptoms
Nocturia two to three times per night
Slow urinary stream
Microscopic hematuria (3–5 red cells per high-power field)
Normal renal ultrasonography findings
Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass
Biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma
Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition
No history of lichen sclerosis, sexually transmitted infection, pelvic radiation, genitourinary trauma, or family history of genitourinary malignancy
Systemic evaluation for amyloidosis revealed no additional disease manifestations
Retrograde urethrography showed an approximately 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra

shortlist.label: Localized Urethral Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition and the patient has a urethral mass

shortlist.label: Urethral stricture
shortlist.why_kept: Retrograde urethrography showed an approximately 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass concerning for urothelial carcinoma, although biopsy was negative

shortlist.label: Primary Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic evaluation for amyloidosis revealed no additional disease manifestations, but primary amyloidosis is still a possibility

shortlist.label: Secondary Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient lacks a history of chronic inflammatory diseases, secondary amyloidosis cannot be completely ruled out

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results are consistent with localized urethral amyloidosis, as evidenced by the presence of a circumferential urethral mass and amyloid protein deposition on biopsy, without any additional disease manifestations or systemic involvement.

rejected.label: Urethral stricture
rejected.why: While the patient has a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra, the presence of amyloid protein deposition suggests a more specific diagnosis than a simple stricture.

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: Biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Primary Amyloidosis
rejected.why: The patient's amyloidosis appears to be localized to the urethra, without any systemic involvement or additional disease manifestations.

rejected.label: Secondary Amyloidosis
rejected.why: The patient lacks a history of chronic inflammatory diseases or other conditions that would suggest secondary amyloidosis, and the amyloidosis is localized to the urethra.
